title: A Noise-Aware Quantum Algorithm for Credit Valuation Adjustments on Real Quantum Hardware
authors: Guillem Borràs Espert, Francisco Gómez Casanova, Luis de Pedro Sánchez, Senaida Hernández Santana, Pablo Serrano Molinero
abstract: Credit Valuation Adjustment (CVA) requires repeated risk-neutral expectation estimation, making it a natural test bed for quantum amplitude estimation, whose coherent amplification can in principle reduce Monte Carlo sampling cost. Whether this advantage survives realistic financial encoding and noisy hardware remains open. We develop an end-to-end, noise-aware quantum workflow for CVA, covering market calibration, discretisation, oracle construction, hardware execution and error-budget analysis. The model combines a correlated two-asset exposure with discount and default factors, encoded through a QCBM-based joint time-market distribution and controlled payoff rotations. We introduce contrast-aware Bayesian iterative quantum amplitude estimation (CABIQAE), which incorporates experimentally calibrated Grover-contrast loss into Bayesian inference and circuit-depth selection. Hardware-calibrated experiments show that CABIQAE exploits the limited amplification available on current devices more effectively than noise-agnostic alternatives and achieves a much lower classical post-processing runtime than the noise-aware BAE baseline. The analysis further decomposes the total CVA error into statistical, encoding, discretisation and hardware contributions. The full CVA oracle remains limited by circuit depth and discretisation resolution.
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive, noise-aware quantum workflow designed to estimate Credit Valuation Adjustments (CVA) using Quantum Amplitude Estimation. The authors introduce CABIQAE, an algorithm that adapts Bayesian inference by incorporating measured hardware contrast loss. While demonstrating improved performance over naive methods on current devices, the work highlights that practical utility is currently constrained by circuit depth and discretization limits.
main_problem: The paper addresses the practical viability of using quantum amplitude estimation (QAE) to accelerate Credit Valuation Adjustment (CVA) calculations on real, noisy quantum hardware.
main_result: A novel noise-aware algorithm, CABIQAE, was shown to exploit limited quantum amplification more effectively than noise-agnostic methods on current devices. However, the overall CVA oracle remains fundamentally limited by circuit depth and discretization resolution.
method: The authors developed an end-to-end workflow incorporating a specialized Bayesian iterative QAE (CABIQAE) that incorporates experimentally calibrated Grover-contrast loss into its inference process.
model_or_system: The financial model involves calculating CVA for correlated two-asset exposures, encoded using a QCBM-based joint time-market distribution. Experiments are performed on real quantum hardware (e.g., IBM Quantum).
key_observables: CVA error decomposition (statistical, encoding, discretisation, hardware), final relative error of the estimator, and circuit resource counts (Logical vs. ISA gates/depth).
important_parameters: Circuit depth, discretization resolution ($n$), query cost ($N_q$), and experimentally calibrated contrast loss parameters.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that a quantum advantage can be extracted despite noise; the work explicitly models hardware limitations rather than assuming ideal coherence.
figures_summary: Figures characterize Grover amplification for toy and CVA circuits, showing empirical contrast decay. Other figures compare the final relative error and runtime of various amplitude estimation techniques under hardware constraints versus ideal theory.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for quantum acceleration in CVA to developing a noise-aware workflow (CABIQAE). It details the financial encoding, presents theoretical guarantees (ideal scaling), validates the approach on real hardware by analyzing resource scaling and error accumulation, and concludes with an error decomposition analysis.
why_interesting: While focused on finance, the core methodology—developing robust quantum algorithms that explicitly account for noise-induced contrast loss during amplitude estimation—is highly relevant to any field using NISQ devices for complex simulation or optimization.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: Figure 1: Quantum encoding of the discretised multi-asset CVA. The unitary GP prepares a coherent superposition over the full time–market grid, while Rv, Rp, and Rq encode the positive exposure, discount factor, and default probability into three dedicated ancillas. The projector Π111 selects the event in which all three ancillas are measured in state |1⟩.
Figure 2: Three-qubit circuit Atest used to validate CABIQAE. The final rotation angle φ is left free to generate different target amplitudes.

Figure 3: Hardware-compatible QCBM ansatz used for the six-qubit state-preparation block. Each variational block combines local single-qubit rotations with parametrised RZZ entanglers placed along a connectivity pattern chosen to respect the target heavy-hex hardware constraints.

Figure 5: CRCA used for the exposure rotation Rv. The displayed outward and inward snake layers route information between the computational register and the exposure ancilla while preserving a hardware-aware entangling structure.
Figure 6: Reduced test-instance amplitude estimation results in the noiseless (top) and hardware-replay (bottom) regimes.
